newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to auction 40 pct of Surgut Holding.
newsitem.headline: Russia to auction 40 pct of Surgut Holding.

text.p: The Russian government will auction 40.12 percent of NK Surgutneftegaz (Surgut Holding) on February 25, the Russian Federal Property Fund said on Tuesday.
The stake amounts to four million shares, it said in the latest issue of its Reforma bulletin.
The stake is currently held in trust by Surgut Holding's pension fund under the government's shares-for-loans scheme.
Surgut Holding is one of a dozen vertically integrated Russian oil groups created over the last few years. Its main operating unit is AO Surgutneftegaz SNGS.RTS 0#SNGS.RUO.

The pension fund won the stake in Surgut Holding in November 1995 in the first transaction under the controversial shares-for-loans scheme, in which investors won the right to manage state-owned shares in partly privatised companies in return for loans to the government.
The pension fund is in turn mostly owned by Surgut Holding.
Next month's auction to transfer ownership of the stake will be the third such sale of stakes acquired in shares-for-loans deals, following auctions of stakes in oil groups YUKOS and SIDANKO.
In both these cases the auctions were won by companies which according to analysts appear to be close to those who won the original shares-for-loans contests.
